# Focused native Windows diagnosis

This isolated branch compiles the reviewed source `f07db3725e185babd7abd6e55942c5e616b01eac`, verifies all 674 discovered names and preservation of every original 666-name baseline, then executes the existing ten Windows-selected methods: InvocationBindingTests (4), CapabilityExecutableSnapshotPoolTests (5), and RCIRReceiptTrustGapTests (1). The seven pool methods remain in source; two preserve their existing non-Windows guards. The runtime Sources tree remains `fd3f153c2a1e195e7766a40a1585f6526c73794a`. It does not replace the complete candidate suite or establish release readiness.

The five named failures in the natural 78ea Windows run remain retained. This source adds fixed fixture/bootstrap stages for the three invocation failures, corrects the owned pool fixture's sealed timestamp setup, and provisions the trust fixture with the existing protected host-file primitive. Original methods and assertion lines remain. The precise invocation failure boundary is pending native measurement. The frozen E39 archive describes the earlier 78ea tests, not this diagnostic assembly.

The runner uses pinned Swift 6.2, Python 3.12 and the unchanged reviewed owned-job supervisor. Build/discovery/focused deadlines are 1200/60/600 seconds. Only the ten-test filter is diagnostic; subsequent release acceptance still requires complete unfiltered platform checks. No release, tag, tap formula, installed runtime or repository settings are changed by this workflow.

Raw child stdout is redirected to runner-private files. Only fixed enum labels, test names, measurements and hashes are published. The full focused test log and a strict allowlist of owned trust export files are size bounded and encrypted with CMS AuthEnvelopedData AES-256-GCM and RSA-OAEP SHA256/MGF1 SHA256 to the pinned public certificate. Symlinks, junctions, unknown files and over-budget files are rejected. Private signing-key material is never in the allowlist. The recipient private key remains off-runner. Unsupported encryption or failed algorithm inspection fails closed without uploading plaintext. Native Windows encryption is pending; the local public-certificate control is not native proof. The recipient independently authenticates and decrypts the downloaded ciphertext before any raw trust verdict is accepted.

The safe artifact contains the summary, owned supervisor phase measurements and authenticated ciphertext only. The receipt keys, arguments, fixture journals and full assertions remain inside ciphertext. Provider-generation values are not projected. Safe stage labels are bound to the observed selected test start/finish intervals; their presence is diagnostic evidence, not a proven runtime defect or external issuer guarantee.
